findings.title: Copy-paste bug: rawTokenId is never null-checked
findings.body: Line 73 checks `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` but should check `rawTokenId` instead of `grantType` again. This means a null `rawTokenId` will not be rejected at construction time and will cause a NullPointerException later (e.g., in `encodeTokenId` when concatenating the string).

findings.title: Inverted logic in isAccessTokenId matcher: returns false when grant shortcut matches
findings.body: The condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false (non-match) when the grant shortcut equals the expected value. This is backwards — it should return false when they are NOT equal (i.e., `!equals`). As written, the matcher rejects tokens that have the correct grant type and accepts tokens with the wrong grant type.

findings.title: Wrong substring index for grant type shortcut in isAccessTokenId
findings.body: The token ID format is `<sessionType:2><tokenType:2><grantType:2>:<uuid>`, so the grant type shortcut occupies characters at indices 4 and 5 (i.e., `substring(4, 6)`). The code uses `substring(3, 5)` which extracts the last character of the token type and the first character of the grant type (e.g., "ta" from "onrtac"). Combined with the inverted logic bug, the matcher never actually validates the grant type, making the test assertions ineffective.

findings.title: Removal of public copy constructor from OAuth2GrantType.Context is a source-incompatible SPI change
findings.body: The copy constructor `Context(Context context)` was removed from `OAuth2GrantType.Context`, which is a public class in the `server-spi-private` module. Any extension or custom grant type that constructs a Context from an existing Context instance will fail to compile after upgrading. This is a breaking API change for SPI consumers.

findings.title: Package-private mutable fields exposed for testing
findings.body: `grantsByShortcuts` and `grantsToShortcuts` are declared with package-private access (no modifier) to allow direct manipulation in the unit test. This bypasses encapsulation and means any class in the same package can mutate these maps. Consider using a test-specific factory setup or making these fields accessible via a protected method instead.
